entry.title: Towards a Unified Framework for Protein Interaction Site Prediction Using Hierarchical Protein Representations
entry.summary:
Proteins interact with a wide range of biomolecular partners, yet identifying the interaction sites that mediate these events remains a major challenge for understanding cellular function and guiding drug discovery. Existing computational methods are typically designed for specific interaction classes and often rely on task-specific features. Here, we introduce PRIME-ISP, a structure-based framework for predicting interaction sites across diverse biomolecular interaction types using a unified architecture.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #number-theory

entry.title: MutaStruct: Revisiting Benchmarks for Single-Site Mutation-Induced Structural Change Prediction
entry.summary:
Predicting the structural consequences of single-site mutations is fundamental to understanding protein function, disease mechanisms, and protein engineering. However, existing benchmarks for mutation-induced structural change prediction are often affected by duplicate mutation events, highly similar structural pairs, and experimental-state confounders, which can inflate reported performance. We introduce MutaStruct, a curated benchmark of experimentally observed single-mutation protein structure pairs designed for rigorous evaluation of mutation-induced structural changes.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: NuFold RNA Structure Database: Large-Scale RNA Tertiary Structure Prediction with Confidence Metrics
entry.summary:
Summary: To bridge the gap between rapid RNA sequence discovery and slow experimental characterization, we present the NuFold RNA Structure Database (https://nufold.kiharalab.org/), a resource providing large-scale, precomputed full-atom RNA tertiary structures. By removing the computational barriers associated with running the method locally, this database makes high-accuracy RNA structure models readily accessible to the biological research community for a wide range of applications. Availability and implementation: All predicted structures and corresponding data are available at https://nufold.kiharalab.org/.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #databases

entry.title: Pose: a pure-NumPy, chirality-aware, structural engine for building and manipulating the molecular structures of proteins, nucleic acids, and small organic molecules
entry.summary:
Molecular modelling protocols often cross several programs, each with its own formats, conventions, and installation, and few treat D-amino acids and other non-canonical residues consistently. This work presents Pose, a Python library whose only run-time dependency is NumPy. Pose builds polypeptides, including six non-canonical amino acids, and nucleic-acid duplexes from sequence, with letter case setting each residue's handedness, and reimplements three force fields (OpenFF Sage 2.3.0, AMBER ff19SB, and CHARMM36) and two score functions (Rosetta REF15 and AutoDock Vina) as readable array operations.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: T2G: fast and accurate transcriptome to genome BAM liftover for short and long read RNA sequencing
entry.summary:
Aligning RNA sequencing reads to the transcriptome rather than the genome recovers short and junction-spanning reads that genome alignment loses or misplaces, but it leaves the alignments in transcript coordinates, which genome browsers, variant callers and most annotation tools cannot use. Existing liftover tools translate between genome assemblies, and the few that reach transcript coordinates are tied to a single quantification model or assay type. Here we describe T2G, which converts complete BAM files from transcriptome to genome coordinates while keeping CIGAR strings, alignment tags and per-base RNA modification calls intact.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: Hybrid modeling for improved structure prediction of large protein complexes
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01067-w An automated framework, HDOCK-Multimer (HDM), is developed that integrates ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly for the structure prediction of large protein complexes.
